records.name: Stimulus Children's Theatre Company
records.summary: Penn's student theatre company. It stages shows for young audiences with lessons about friendship, acceptance, and kindness, and it does community service for Philadelphia youth.
records.what_you_do: Audition for a show, interview for a tech crew spot, or sign up for the community service team.

schedule.text: Fall 2026 musical auditions were on August 29 and 30, with tech interviews on September 6 and 8

first_step.how: Email the board address in the directory to ask about the next audition or the community service team
first_step.basis: Shows need auditions and tech interviews, but community service is joined by email

records.notes: The group's own site has no posts newer than 2018, so the 2026 status comes from the Penn Clubs entry. The audition dates in that entry are for the fall 2026 season and have passed.

records.name: Strictly Funk
records.summary: Penn's student hip-hop and contemporary dance company, founded in 1997. It mixes jazz, lyrical, and funk styles.
records.what_you_do: Attend the workshops and auditions the group posts at the start of each semester, then dance with the company.

first_step.how: Watch for the start of semester workshop and audition dates, or email the board
first_step.basis: The directory mentions auditions each semester, so joining may depend on one

records.notes: No own website is listed and no dated post was found. The status rests on the directory marking the group as accepting members.

records.name: Student-Athlete Investment Club
records.summary: A club for Penn student-athletes who want to learn investing basics and build long-term financial skills.
records.what_you_do: Learn how investing works alongside other student-athletes.

first_step.how: Apply through the club's homepage, as the directory describes
first_step.basis: Joining takes an application, and the group is open to varsity and club student-athletes

records.notes: Open to varsity and club student-athletes per the directory, so open_to is students. No own website or dated item found. The directory gives only JMHH as the location.

records.name: Student-Athletes in Medicine
records.summary: A group for Penn student-athletes who want careers in medicine or healthcare. It offers networking, learning resources, and mentoring.
records.what_you_do: Meet other athletes on medical career paths, use the group's resources, and connect with mentors.

first_step.how: Email the club or follow its Instagram to ask how to join

records.notes: No own website and no dated item. The directory lists the group as accepting members. Application status is not recorded because the directory flag is a bare number with no label.

records.name: Student Harm Reduction Coalition
records.summary: A student group at Penn that works on addiction in Philadelphia through education, tabling, and volunteer outreach with partner groups.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer on clinical outreach with partner groups, and help with education and tabling about harm reduction.

first_step.how: Applications open at the student activities fair (the SAC fair), so subscribe to the newsletter for dates
first_step.basis: The group needs an application, and the directory says it is not accepting members right now

records.notes: Status is unknown. The group's site shows no dated posts, only a 2023 footer and 2023 image file names, and the directory's application note has no year. Confirm before relying on it.

records.name: Student Planning Association (SPA)
records.summary: The official student group for planning and urban affairs students at Penn. It runs professional development, social events, and a place to share planning resources.
records.what_you_do: Come to the group's events, which are open to the public, or join as a university student to take part in its work.

first_step.how: Go to a public event first, or email the group to ask how to become a member
first_step.basis: Events are open to the public and membership is open to any university student, though the page does not say how to sign up

records.notes: The group's page lists a different contact email (PennDesignSPA@gmail.com). The directory email is recorded here. No event dates are shown on either page.

records.name: Students at Penn for Sports Fitness and Health in West Philadelphia Schools
records.summary: Penn student volunteers who bring sports, fitness, and health education to students in West Philadelphia schools.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer in West Philadelphia schools, helping kids with sports, fitness, and health activities.

first_step.how: Fill out the online membership form linked from the directory entry
first_step.basis: Any Penn student can join through the online membership form

records.notes: No own website and no dated item. The membership form is the only way-in step found.

records.name: Students Providing Aid (SPAid@PENN)
records.summary: The Penn chapter of a national student group. Members build kid-friendly first aid kits and share them with communities that need them.
records.what_you_do: Apply, interview with the officers, and then take part in kit building, fundraising, and volunteer events.

first_step.how: Fill out the interest form linked in the directory, then complete the online application and a virtual interview
first_step.basis: Membership needs an online application and a virtual interview with the officers

records.notes: The national site has no page for the Penn chapter, so chapter dates are unconfirmed. The directory lists no events.

records.name: Sustainability Consulting at Penn
records.summary: A student-run consulting group that gives free sustainability advice to organizations, with projects in the Americas, Australia, and Europe.
records.what_you_do: Join a consulting team and work on pro bono sustainability projects for clients.

first_step.how: Fill out the Fall 2026 interest form and apply during the fall application
first_step.basis: Members join through the fall application, and the directory marks the group as not accepting members outside that process

records.notes: The directory says the group is not accepting members, yet it also says the Fall 2026 application is open. The record uses the application wording. The group's site footer reads 2024, which is not used as evidence, and its pages show no dated items.

records.name: Tabletop at Penn
records.summary: A Penn group for people who play tabletop role-playing games, especially Dungeons and Dragons.
records.what_you_do: Play tabletop role-playing games with other members at the group's weekly Saturday meeting.

first_step.how: Come to a Saturday meeting at 1 pm, or email the group first
first_step.basis: The directory says membership is open at any level of commitment, and the group meets every week

records.notes: The directory says anyone can be a member, but it is not clear whether that includes non-students, so open_to is students. No website and no dated item found.

records.name: Taekwondo Club (ITF)
records.summary: Penn's traditional taekwondo club, founded in 1985. It focuses on physical and mental training with no competition.
records.what_you_do: Attend Monday, Wednesday, or Friday classes during the school semesters, and get one-to-one help with basic technique as a beginner.

schedule.text: Classes on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday during the fall and spring semesters; start times are not published

first_step.how: Email the club to ask questions, or come to any open class
first_step.basis: The club says beginners are welcome in every class and gives basic instruction one to one

records.notes: The club's site has no dated posts and a 2015 footer, which is not used as evidence. Cost is not stated anywhere. The site lists no class start times, and the locations change by term and in warm weather.

records.name: Taekwondo Club (World Taekwondo) at Penn
records.summary: Penn's World Taekwondo club. It welcomes students at every skill level and takes part in a college league.
records.what_you_do: Train at the Pottruck studio several times a week, and join league competitions if you want to compete.

schedule.text: Spring 2026 schedule: Sunday 11 am to 1 pm, and Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday 7:30 to 9:30 pm

first_step.how: Email the club or message on Instagram or Facebook, then complete the mandatory Fusion Club waiver before a first practice
first_step.basis: The club says no experience is needed and welcomes drop-ins at any practice

records.notes: The site says it was last updated in January 2026 for the spring semester, so times may have changed. The directory says graduates are welcome too. Audience is recorded as students.

records.name: Taiwanese Society at Penn
records.summary: A group for Penn students who care about Taiwanese culture and affairs. It holds dinners, social nights, and cultural events that are also open to the wider Penn community.
records.what_you_do: Sign up to get event discounts and a t-shirt, then come to dinners, socials, and cultural events.

first_step.how: Fill out the sign-up form listed in the directory entry
first_step.basis: Any Penn student can sign up through the form, and events are open to the wider Penn community

records.notes: The group's website did not load (the lookup failed on both forms of the address), so no dated events were checked. The only date in the directory is a sign-up link named for the 2024 to 2025 year, which is not used as evidence. The heritage list has no Taiwanese tag, so no heritage code was set.

records.name: Taiwanese Student Association at Penn
records.summary: A graduate and professional student group at Penn. It builds community and cultural ties around Taiwanese affairs through social, cultural, learning, and career events.
records.what_you_do: Join socials and cultural or career events with other graduate students, and get in touch through the group's social pages.

first_step.how: Message the group on Facebook or Instagram to ask how to get involved
first_step.basis: The directory lists the group as accepting members and gives social media contacts, though no joining steps are described

records.notes: No website and no dated item. Facts come from the directory entry only. The group is for graduate and professional students, so open_to is students.

records.name: TEDxPenn
records.summary: A student-run group that puts on a large TEDx conference at Penn.
records.what_you_do: Join one of five teams (speakers and content, operations, design, marketing, or finance), or nominate a speaker through the group's form.

first_step.how: Attend an information session, then apply through the form for one of the five teams
first_step.basis: Joining takes an information session and an application, and the directory marks the group as not accepting members

records.notes: The site names a 2027 conference, with theme, date, and speakers still to be announced. The directory says 1,000 or more attendees are planned for spring. Whether the conference is open to the public is not stated, so open_to is students. Status is probably_active because the site has no dated post.

records.name: The Alt Protein Project at Penn
records.summary: The Penn chapter of a student network focused on alternative proteins. It offers learning material, research chances, and links to food startups.
records.what_you_do: Take part in the chapter's learning material and research work, and connect with the startup world once accepted.

first_step.how: Applications run in a set window each fall (the Fall 2026 window ran from August 25 to September 3); email the chapter to ask about the next one
first_step.basis: Membership needs an application during a set window

records.notes: The directory lists two named student contacts for applications. Their personal emails are left out, and the club's group email is recorded. The site shows no dated posts, only a 2024 footer. No food-science tag exists, so the group is filed under climate action and stem outreach.

records.name: The Andean Representation
records.summary: A Penn group that shares Andean culture through cultural, academic, and social events. It works with the Quechua at Penn language program.
records.what_you_do: Go to the group's events, and sign up through its interest form for the 2026 to 2027 academic year.

first_step.how: Fill out the group's interest form for the 2026 to 2027 academic year (link in the directory entry)
first_step.basis: Any student can fill out the interest form, and the directory marks the group as accepting members

records.notes: The interest form for the 2026 to 2027 academic year is the only dated item. It shows no month, so no last_sign_of_life is set. No website is listed.

records.name: The Appétit
records.summary: Penn's student-run food magazine. Its articles cover food and recipes.
records.what_you_do: Write for the magazine or join its staff when joining opens, usually in early September or late January.

first_step.how: Use the apply page on the magazine's site when joining opens in early September or late January
first_step.basis: Staff joins through an application that opens at set times, and the site does not describe the steps

records.notes: Article pages show no visible dates, so activity is not confirmed by a dated item. The site's footer reads 2025, which is not used as evidence. The foodie_meetups tag is a loose fit for a magazine.

records.name: The Black Scientist Collective
records.summary: A Penn student group that builds community for Black students who want research careers. It offers networking, career development, and mentoring.
records.what_you_do: Connect with other Black students on research career paths and take part in career development and mentoring.

first_step.how: Email the group to ask how to join; the directory does not describe a joining step

records.notes: The directory has no joining text and no website. The community tag is set from the directory description of who the group serves. Check whether membership is limited before relying on it.

records.name: The Christian Association Student Community
records.summary: An ecumenical Christian campus ministry for students. It offers weekly meals and discussion, service projects, and faith conversations, and it welcomes people of any religious background.
records.what_you_do: Come to the Wednesday dinner and discussion, the monthly Night Church gathering, or another weekly group.

schedule.text: Wednesday dinner and discussion, 6:30 to 8 pm, starting in early September 2026

first_step.how: Come to the Wednesday dinner or join the mailing list on the group's site
first_step.basis: The group says it welcomes every person regardless of religious background and lists a simple way to start

records.notes: The site gives two start dates for the Wednesday dinner, Sept 2 and Sept 6. Sept 2, 2026 is a Wednesday and Sept 6, 2026 is a Sunday, so the record says early September. The directory names SPARC as the weekly meeting place, but the site gives 3637 Chestnut St. Open to the public because the site says every person is welcome. The faith tag is left out because the group is ecumenical. Night Church, Slanguage, and the grad book group are its programs, not separate groups.

blocked.note: Not a bot block: the site did not resolve (DNS lookup failed on the www and bare host). The Taiwanese Society at Penn record is status unknown for this reason.

notes: All 20 directory entries in batch 19 were checked and 20 records were written: 20 publish, 0 hide, 0 duplicate. Fetches used: 33 of 60 (20 Penn Clubs entries, 13 group sites or pages). Searches used: 0. No rate limiting seen; one unreachable site, listed under blocked. Status: active for 6 (Stimulus, Penn World Taekwondo, Sustainability Consulting, Alt Protein, Andean Representation, Christian Association), probably_active for 12, unknown for 2 (Student Harm Reduction Coalition, Taiwanese Society). Eight records rest on the directory entry alone with no dated item and no own site (Strictly Funk, Student-Athlete Investment Club, Student-Athletes in Medicine, Students at Penn for Sports Fitness, Students Providing Aid, Tabletop at Penn, Taiwanese Student Association, Black Scientist Collective). The directory's application flag is an unlabeled number that does not match its own text in several entries, so application status follows the directory text instead. Two student contact emails on the Alt Protein entry and all personal names were left out. Where a directory listing and the group's own site disagree (Sustainability Consulting, TEDxPenn, Stimulus), the record notes it.
